Shall I proceed?' and then executing on approval; the editor is the post-approval turn that creates a real skill file with skill_manage. The first recording routed the editor turn through skill_manage(action='create') because this install exposed no workspace file tool at all - config-gated, not absent, by terminal.backend: docker in the recording home's config.yaml while the Docker daemon was down (36-tool roster). With Docker running the roster is 43 tools and the file toolset is back, so the editor turn now does what the scenario says: write_file CREATES /Users/ingo/hermes-local/workspace/irr-5-4-mycli/mycli.py and patch then EDITS that existing file in place (0.1.0 -> 0.2.0). Two calls, deliberately - creating alone would prove hermes can write a file, not that it can EDIT a project source file, which was exactly the claim the substitution left unproven. The path is absolute and sits under an identity bind-mount from terminal.docker_volumes because the file tools run inside the container and the run cwd is not mounted; that is what makes the artifact verifiable on the host. Neither tool is approval-gated (check_all_command_guards is imported only by tools/terminal_tool.py), so the implement phase is ungated by construction. Hermes writes NO transcript file; the daemon observes the one shared store at $HERMES_HOME/state.db via agent.ProcessOwnedStore. THE CHAIN: (1) the /plan expansion lands as a `user` row -> user_message -> the classifier's total default transcript_activity -> working; (2) the plan turn's role='assistant' finish_reason='stop' row carries the ask, and parser.go computes PendingWaitingCue from the FULL text before truncation while rewriting the SAME row to turn_done, so classifyAgentDone checks IsWaitingForUserInput BEFORE routing to ready and the session goes working->waiting with no ready in between; (3) THE LEG THIS CELL ADDS - the approval reply lands as another `user` row and metrics.go's messageFold.apply explicitly resets pendingWaitingCue ('a new user message answers whatever the agent was waiting on') and clears open tools, so IsAgentDone goes false, no higher ladder rule claims the pass (hermes has no hook tier, no permission-pending signal), and transcript_activity fires waiting->working; (4) the implement turn's cue-free stop row settles working->ready. text: The hermes session appears in ready. UNPINNED: the `sessions` row is INSERTed on the first user message (the /plan expansion), not at launch, so the ready birth comes from the transient proc-<PID> presession the processlifecycle scanner mints - it must not steal the identity the arc lands on.

ARCHITECT / plan phase. The /plan turn drives the hermes session ready -> working: the expanded skill invocation lands as a `user` row and message_count grows while the newest row is not assistant/finish_reason='stop'. The turn spans many 2s poll ticks (the model reads a ~6k-token skill body and writes the plan file under .hermes/plans/), so the working leg is observed on its own merits rather than via catch-up synthesis.

The plan-approval gate. The agent saves the plan and ends the turn asking whether to proceed; that turn-boundary row (assistant/finish_reason='stop') carries the ask, so PendingWaitingCue and turn_done arrive together and classifyAgentDone routes working -> waiting, never through ready. The 'no ready before approval' invariant is enforced STRUCTURALLY by the phase chain rather than by a window invariant - plan_gate is the first waiting after architect_plan(working), editor_implement the first working after plan_gate, turn_end the first ready after editor_implement - so the ordering itself proves no ready interposed. A 'no state_transition to ready' invariant would be WRONG here: unlike 2.18, this cell DOES go ready after approval.

EDITOR / implement phase - the leg 2.18 does not have. The user approves with an ordinary message (hermes' gate is prose, not a modal, so no keystroke primitive is involved). That `user` row resets the waiting cue and clears open tools in messageFold.apply, IsAgentDone goes false, and the classifier's transcript_activity default drives waiting -> working on the SAME session that gated. The agent then makes the editor's two real contributions: write_file creates /Users/ingo/hermes-local/workspace/irr-5-4-mycli/mycli.py and patch edits that same existing file in place (0.1.0 -> 0.2.0). Both land as assistant rows with finish_reason='tool_calls', each closed by a `tool` row on the matching tool_call_id. Note that `write_file` - unlike the skill_manage this cell used before it was re-recorded - IS in isPermissionGatedEditTool's fold-exact set, so an open write_file can emit an extra OpenToolStalled waiting inside this phase; the relative phase chain absorbs it, since turn_end is the FIRST ready after this phase.

The implement turn finishes: an assistant/finish_reason='stop' row whose text carries NO trailing question, so agent_done routes working -> ready. Final state is ready. Ending in waiting instead would mean either the model closed on a question (a recipe/prompt failure) or the run stopped at the gate - the latter being a duplicate of 2.18 and a failure of this cell.
